gna_model: D4 position-7 (S)-GNA modeled as a disrupted Watson-Crick pair (g7 A->C in the seed, UAUAGAG->UAUAGCG); ViennaRNA has no GNA sugar parameters, so this is an explicit destabilization model (upper bound on the GNA penalty), applied to the SAME real Rnor_6.0 3'UTR sites used for D1.
input_definition: e_dG[gene] = sum over canonical 3'UTR sites of min(dG_site, 0) (kcal/mol, negative = direct seed repression, parallel to -seed_match_count).

discrimination.ks_finding: The one-sided KS is RANK-based and saturates (~0.995) for BOTH the count and e_dG: every seed-matched gene keeps a nonzero propagated repression against an exactly-zero background, so the rank separation is near-complete regardless of magnitude. KS cannot discriminate the guides from the propagated signal.
discrimination.magnitude_finding: The MAGNITUDE-sensitive readout (mean propagated repression on seed-matched nodes) carries the discrimination: e_dG gives the parent D1 a stronger predicted effect (-3.610) than the GNA variant D4 (-1.668), a 2.16x ratio, whereas the count gives D1 and D4 the IDENTICAL value (-0.651 vs -0.651). The thermodynamic input separates the chemistries; the rank-based KS metric is what hides it.
discrimination.dose_blind_note: e_dG depends only on the guide chemistry, so D1_10 == D1_30 predicted (same guide D1: pred_ks_dG 0.995 vs 0.994). The thermodynamic input separates the two CHEMISTRIES (D1 vs D4) but is dose-blind: it cannot reproduce the low-dose drop in the measured KS, which is a dose effect, not a seed-thermodynamic one.
